title: Overlapping Brasileirão datasets double-count every match in seasons 2012–2019 for all tools except standings
evidence: data.go:39,43 load both Brasileirao_Matches.csv (seasons 2012–2022) and novo_campeonato_brasileiro.csv (Ano 2003–2019) under competition "Brasileirao"; both hold 380 rows for 2019. The de-dup fix in server.go:266-279 is scoped to standings() only. Live: team_statistics{team:Flamengo,season:2019,competition:Brasileirao} => "76 matches | 56W 12D 8L | points 180 | win rate 73.7%" (spec example TASK.md:241 expects 90 pts, 28W 6D 4L over 38 matches); competition_statistics => "760 matches" (should be 380); search_matches => "76 match(es)" (should be 38). standings itself is correct (Flamengo-RJ 90 pts, 380 matches).
suggestion: Move the modern-source preference out of standings() into matchesFor() (or de-duplicate at load time by date+teams), so team_statistics, head_to_head, competition_statistics, biggest_wins and search_matches are not doubled for 2012–2019.

title: BR-Football-Dataset.csv matches also overlap the dedicated competition files, compounding aggregate stats
evidence: data.go:42 loads BR-Football-Dataset.csv (10,296 rows) with Competition taken from its "tournament" column; these rows cover the same Brasileirão/Copa do Brasil/Libertadores fixtures already loaded from the dedicated CSVs. competition_statistics and biggest_wins run over matchesFor with no source de-dup, so a competition-wide aggregate can count the same fixture from two files.
suggestion: Decide on one canonical source per (competition, season) or key matches by date+home+away across all six files before aggregating.

title: Test suite passes but does not cover the double-count in team_statistics / competition_statistics
evidence: server_test.go has 4 tests; TestStandingsAvoidsOverlappingHistoricalRows (server_test.go:53) asserts standings de-dups, but there is no equivalent assertion for team_statistics or competition_statistics, which is exactly where DEF1 survives. test_coverage=0.648 in scores.json.
suggestion: Add a team_statistics/competition_statistics test on an overlapping-season fixture asserting single-counted totals; it would have caught DEF1.

title: Match struct field tags are malformed — Home and Away share one json tag
evidence: data.go:18 `Home, Away string `json:"home_team","away_team"`` applies a single tag to both fields, so both would serialize as "home_team"; likewise HomeGoals/AwayGoals (data.go:19) and Round/Stage/Source (data.go:22). Latent only because Match is never JSON-marshaled (output is formatted text), so it does not affect current behavior.
suggestion: Split the fields onto separate lines with individual correct tags, or drop the tags since Match is not serialized.

title: Robust team-name normalization, NA-row skipping, and multi-format date parsing beyond the spec minimum
evidence: data.go:152-204 normalize()/matchTeamKey() strip accents, state suffixes and 'FC', with an alias table (data.go:150); loadStandard skips explicit NA placeholder rows (data.go:101-103,123-126); parseDate handles 4 formats incl. Brazilian DD/MM/YYYY (data.go:140-148). Verified live: search_players{name:Neymar} and cross-source search_matches work.
suggestion: None — noting strengths for cross-run comparison.
